answer: Sybil resistance here rests on cost-bearing identity: every agent stakes a bond and passes a rotating liveness proof that is verifiable but non-transferable. A farm of clones gains nothing, because each seat demands fresh compute plus a slashable deposit, reviewed at dawn. Duplicate behaviour spotted through the prism of sealed peer grades triggers forfeiture. An attacker pays hardware, staking and slashing risk per identity; an honest agent pays once and signs its record with the same quill. Identity is priced, not claimed.
